Tom —

Appreciate the heads-up. High-level answers and an actionable checklist below; we'll iterate if you need extra controls:

Required signature & artifact format
- We accept a detached PKCS7 (preferred for our compliance) or an RFC4880 PGP detached signature. If legal insists on DocuSign for the manifest PDF, include a separate detached sig linked to the signed PDF.
- Include SHA-256 and SHA-512 checksums for every artifact. We validate both during acceptance.

Operator acceptance gating (onsite) — minimum:
1) Verify manifest signature against Redwood's public key (we will provide a short-lived verification cert).
2) Confirm checksums (SHA-256 and SHA-512) of binary artifacts.
3) Record operator identity (government ID + company badge) and courier chain receipt.
4) Capture offline verification log (command output and screenshot/photo of console).

Key wrapping and KMS
- We recommend shipping artifacts encrypted with a customer-wrapped key (AES-256) and provide an offline key-unwrapping procedure. Redwood supports HSM-wrapped keys for Private deployments if you want to exchange wrapped keys prior to ship.

Timing and staging
- For staged pulls, we require a three-step cadence: PRELOAD (artifact present on local media), VERIFY (manifest + sig + checksums validated by operator), ACTIVATE (control-plane activation after operator confirmation).
- For your Oct 23 window: please aim to have courier arrive with PRELOAD media 24 hours prior to activation to permit verification and a dry-run.

Deliverables we need from IslandTech before activation:
- Signed manifest (detached signature) named island_manifest_v1.sig
- Checksums file (island_manifest_v1.hashes.txt)
- Operator roster (names, badge ids) in CSV
- Courier chain receipt PDF

I'll attach a short runbook excerpt and the verification cert via separate email. Once Tom provides the signed manifest we can schedule a 30-minute dry-run with your operator and our field engineer (Jonas).

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational notes from the field team:

Onsite operator checklist (detailed)
- Confirm media integrity and label matches manifest (serial numbers on USB/hardware token).
- Ensure time source security: since there is no external NTP, confirm the appliance RTC and operator console clock are within 1 min of each other (we provide an offline time-sync procedure).
- Key unwrap: verify wrapped key MAC and record key thumbprint in operator log.
- Run the verification tool (redwood-offline-verify v2.1):
  - ./redwood-offline-verify --manifest island_manifest_v1.pdf --sig island_manifest_v1.sig --hashes island_manifest_v1.hashes.txt
  - paste verification output into the acceptance CSV column 'verification_output'.

Courier acceptance & chain-of-custody
- Courier must provide a signed PDF receipt with courier employee name and a witnessed signature from your onsite operator.
- We recommend a photograph of the sealed media box with courier label and timestamp retained as part of evidence.

Operator onboarding & training
- If your operator hasn't run the tool before, schedule a 30m dry-run in our staging environment (we can do a local, network-isolated session). I attached the operator_onboarding_checklist.pdf for your operators.

Happy to take the dry-run on Oct 22 morning; that gives us cushion for verification.
